IOHN.|223}}</noinclude>mai{{ls}}ter in I{{ls}}rael, and art thou ignorant of the{{ls}}e things? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=11}} Amen, Amen I {{ls}}ay to thee, that we {{ls}}peake that vvhich vve knovv, and that vvhich vve haue {{ls}}een vve te{{ls}}tifie, and our te{{ls}}timonie you receiue not. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=12}} If I haue {{ls}}poken to you earthly things, and you beleeue not: hovv if I {{ls}}hal {{ls}}peake to you heauenly things, vvil you beleeue? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=13}} And no man hath a{{ls}}cended into heauen, but he that de{{ls}}cended from heauen, the Sonne of man vvhich is in heauen. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=14}} And as {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Nu. 21, 9.''}}* Moy{{ls}}es exalted the {{ls}}erpent in the de{{ls}}ert, {{ls}}o mu{{ls}}t the Sonne of man be exalted: {{verse|chapter=3|verse=15}} that euery one vvhich beleeueth in him, peri{{ls}}h not, but may haue life euerla{{ls}}ting. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=16}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō Munday in the whit{{ls}}onweeke.}}For {{ls}}o God loued the vvorld, that he gaue his only-begotten {{ls}}onne: that euery one that beleeueth in him, peri{{ls}}h not, but may haue life euerla{{ls}}ting.⊣ {{verse|chapter=3|verse=17}} For God {{ls}}ent not his {{ls}}onne into the vvorld, to iudge the vvorld, but that the vvorld may be {{ls}}aued by him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=18}} He that beleeueth in him, is not iudged. but he that doeth not beleeue, {{sup|‖}} is already iudged: becau{{ls}}e he hath not beleeued in the name of the only-begotten {{ls}}onne of God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=19}} And this is the iudgment: becau{{ls}}e the light is come into the vvorld, and men haue loued the darkene{{ls}}{{ls}}e rather then the light: for their vvorkes vvere euil. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=20}} For euery one that doeth il, hateth the light, and commeth not to the light, that his vvorkes may not be controuled. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=21}} But he that doeth veritie, commeth to the light, that his vvorkes may be made manife{{ls}}t, becau{{ls}}e they vvere done in God.⊣

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=22}} After the{{ls}}e things {{sc|Iesvs}} came and his Di{{ls}}ciples into the countrie of Ievvrie: and there he abode vvith them, and baptized. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=23}} And Iohn al{{ls}}o vvas baptizing in Aenon be{{ls}}ide Salim: becau{{ls}}e there vvas much vvater there, and they came, and vvere baptized. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=24}} For Iohn vvas not yet ca{{ls}}t into pri{{ls}}on. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=25}} And there ro{{ls}}e a que{{ls}}tion of Iohns di{{ls}}ciples vvith the Ievves concerning purification. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=26}} And they came to Iohn, and {{ls}}aid to him, Rabbi, he that vvas vvith thee beyond Iordan, to vvhom {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 1, 19.''}}* thou did{{ls}}t giue te{{ls}}timonie, behold he baptizeth, and al come to him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=27}} Iohn an{{ls}}vvered and {{ls}}aid, A man can not receiue any thing, vnle{{ls}}{{ls}}e it be giuen him from heauen. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=28}} Your {{ls}}elues doe beare me vvitne{{ls}}{{ls}}e, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 1, 20.''}}* that I {{ls}}aid, I am not {{sc|Christ}}: but that I am {{ls}}ent before him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=29}} He that hath the bride, is the bridegrome: but the frende of the bridegrome that {{ls}}tandeth and heareth him, reioyceth vvith ioy for the voice of the bridegrome. This my ioy therfore is {{hws|fil|filled.}}<noinclude>{{rh|||led.}}</noinclude>
